consequence.statement: RBAC policies that use the Dex sub claim as the subject no longer match the user, so those users lose the access the policies granted.
consequence.remediation: Update the RBAC policies to use the user_id value (decode the current sub claims to find it), and use the new CLI version to obtain tokens with the appropriate claims.

original.statement: With Dex SSO, Argo CD 3.0 bases the RBAC subject on the federated_claims.user_id claim (requesting the federated:id scope) instead of the sub claim, so RBAC policies that reference the Dex sub claim must be updated to keep the same access.

decision.reason: [ev-0b6150153730] says Argo CD now uses the `federated_claims.user_id` claim as the RBAC subject instead of the Dex `sub` claim. It also says that if you were using the Dex `sub` claim in RBAC policies, "you will need to update them to maintain the same access". So if the operator does nothing, those policies stop matching and users lose the access the policies gave them. That makes permission-lost (action) the right kind, and the proposed statement and remediation (decode the `sub` claims to find the `user_id`, then use the new CLI) match the evidence.
